{{c|''Ananias and his vvife Saphira, for their {{ls}}acrilege, at Peters word fall downe dead, to the great terrour of the re{{ls}}t. 12 By the Apo{{ls}}tles miracles, not onely the number, but al{{ls}}o their faith {{ls}}o increa{{ls}}eth, that they {{ls}}eeke in the {{ls}}treates to the very {{ls}}hadow of Peter, the townes al{{ls}}o about bringing their di{{ls}}ea{{ls}}ed to Hieru{{ls}}alem. 17 The Rulers againe oppo{{ls}}e them {{ls}}elues, but in vaine. 19 For out of pri{{ls}}on an Angel deliuereth them, bidding them preach openly to al: 27 and in their Councel Peter is nothing afraid of their bigge wordes: 34 Yea Gamaliel being one of them {{ls}}elues ca{{ls}}teth a doubt among them, le{{ls}}t the matter be of God, and therfore impo{{ls}}sible to be di{{ls}}{{ls}}olued. 40 Finally, the Apo{{ls}}tles being {{ls}}courged by them, count it an honour, and cea{{ls}}e no day from preaching.''}} {{dropinitial|B|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial B, heads among foliage.png|imgsize=235px|fl={{verse|chapter=5|verse=1}}}}VT a certaine man named Ananias, vvith Saphîra his vvife {{ls}}old a peece of land, {{verse|chapter=5|verse=2}}† and {{sup|‖}} defrauded of the price of the land, his vvife being priuie thereto: and bringing a certaine portion, laide it at the feete of the Apo{{ls}}tles. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=3}}† And {{sup|‖}} Peter {{ls}}aid, Ananias, vvhy hath Satan tempted thy hart, that thou {{ls}}houlde{{ls}}t lie to the holy<noinclude>{{rh|||Gho{{ls}}t,}}</noinclude>
